answer: Admission is capped at 5 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm therefore spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the terrace quota and the lantern admission check. Because the walnut audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 38 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
